measurement.form: four attempts of ONE run on ONE commit — ADR-019 §5's own form

derivation.rule: ADR-013 Decision 3 — slowest observed +15%, rounded up to a multiple of five — applied through `eval_adapter._band_rule`, the same function `ci-numbers-are-derived` uses
derivation.note_on_the_earlier_figure: The 125 reported last round came from attempt 1 alone (105.14). Re-derived from the table's maximum as instructed; it lands on 125 again, but from 107.89, not carried forward.

R7.invariant_ceiling_moved: Yes — 20 -> 25, and the orchestrator was right that I had wrongly called this settled. CI's invariant run was never over budget and still is not; the ceiling moves because it is a DERIVED number and the tree deriving it grew from 48 cases to 74. Deriving fast from the new table while leaving invariant on the old one would publish two trees inside one table — the class this PR spent five rounds closing.
changed: ADR-019 §5: table replaced with run 32937020758's four attempts, cited by run id and commit, hand-read per `gh run view ... --attempt N --log`; both derivations shown; the two paragraphs that argued from the retired 116-case table are struck in place with a dated pointer rather than deleted.

ADR-019 §5: the re-run caveat recorded ONCE, as instructed — four attempts of one run sample the runner's variance but hold commit, image and allocation fixed, so it is a narrower sample than the attempt count suggests; §6's no-ratchet-down rule is what makes publishing from it safe (a short sample is a lower bound).
.github/workflows/eval.yml: comment-block cells replaced (attempt order, both suites) and EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST 90 -> 125, EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_INVARIANT 20 -> 25.
README.md: the bolded four-value fast list, the run id, both min-max ranges and both derived ceilings — all read back from §5's table by `ci-numbers-are-derived`.

evals/adversarial/fast-wall-clock-budget.json: `ci_wall_seconds` 90 -> 125 and `ci_invariant_wall_seconds` 20 -> 25; this case pins what the workflow DECLARES, while `ci-numbers-are-derived` ties those declarations back to §5's cells.

ADR-029 §2: CI is measured across four attempts, both ceilings are derived, and the section states that it supersedes BOTH of its earlier positions — the 'UNMEASURED / local-only' scoping and the 'deliberately red CI wall clock' framing.

red_first.note: The red names every copy that had to move, which is the point of the check: one edit to the graded table reddened all eight surfaces at once.
red_first.second_red: fast-wall-clock-budget, once the workflow moved and the case had not: {"workflow": "EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST", "declared": "125", "expected": 90} and the same for INVARIANT at 25 against 20.

gate.ci_confirmation: The CI run of the commit carrying these ceilings is the check on the number and is read after the push, not asserted here.
